title: Finitely generated cancellative torsion-free monoids have unique sums
statement: Let $M$ be a finitely generated commutative monoid written additively with identity $0$, using the additive monoid convention of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Assume cancellation: $x+z=y+z$ implies $x=y$, and torsion freeness: $nx=ny$ for an integer $n>0$ implies $x=y$. For every pair of nonempty finite subsets $A,B\subseteq M$ there exist $a_0\in A$ and $b_0\in B$ such that, for $a\in A$ and $b\in B$, the equality $a+b=a_0+b_0$ implies $a=a_0$ and $b=b_0$. Here $nx$ means the sum of $n$ copies of $x$.
